messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Production p99 latency spike detected for /v1/generate in us-west-2. Error rate + KV cache growth anomaly. Current p99 = 1.8s (> SLO 0.9s). Link: https://dash.redwood/internal/alerts/1823045678 :rotating_light:
Alex: paging oncall now. i'm on it — checking tail of logs and recent deploys.
Priya: saw a config roll ~5m ago: continuous_batching.enable=true on runtime pool 'rwd-gpu-a'. who rolled?
Mateo: that was me, quick perf tweak for throughput. i tested on staging, didn't see cache blowup. rolling out canaryed to 20% then promoted.
Lina: bumping customer tickets — a few reports of slow chat responses, not total failures. cc @Carlos for customer comms.
Alex: okay — steering: first, can we toggle continuous batching off for affected pool and observe? we should also raise HPA min replicas while we stabilize.
Mateo: on it. backing out canary now. running:
```
# disable continuous batching for pool
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  https://api.redwood.internal/pools/rwd-gpu-a/config -d '{"continuous_batching":false}'
```
Alex: 👍 do we have a quick rollback for the runtime config?
Mateo: done. API returned 204. patch applied at 1823045742.
SREBot: HPA event: rwd-gpu-a scaled from 3 -> 6 replicas at 1823045760 due to CPU surge.
Priya: i'm also patching the HPA min to 4 to avoid instant scale-down during warmup: `kubectl patch hpa rwd-gpu-a -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":4}}'`
Alex: good. watch latency and KV cache size metric (kv.kv_cache.entries). Lina — note for support: impact window ~1823045600- . We'll update once stable.
Lina: on it. drafting status: "Intermittent latency affecting chat responses in US-WEST. Engineering rolling back recent batching change; working on stabilization."
Mateo: spawning a lightweight cache trim job to clear stale prefixes while warmup happens. running:
```
python tools/kv_admin.py --pool rwd-gpu-a --action trim --age 300
```
Carlos: customers asking if we expect data loss — please state no user data loss and that this is performance config.
Alex: good point. include that in comms.
SREBot: kv.kv_cache.entries for rwd-gpu-a peaked at 18M -> trimmed to 1.2M after job at 1823045890.
Priya: latency p99 dropped to 0.95s after rollback and trim. still above SLO but trending down.
Mateo: enabling a temporary throttle on batch size to reduce amplification: config patch:
```
{ "batching": { "max_batch_size": 8, "max_tokens_per_batch": 2048 } }
```
applied at 1823045975.
Alex: monitoring. also enabling kv warmup hysteresis to avoid HPA thrash: `hpa.metrics.kv_cache_delta_threshold=0.15` set on autoscaler controller.
Priya: note: we observed scaling oscillation when continuous batching was previously enabled. hysteresis should give a 30s stabilization window. applied at 1823046002.
Lina: updated support note: "Mitigation in progress. We've rolled back the batching change and applied protective throttles. Some customers may see improved latency within minutes."
Carlos: queued a customer-facing post for impacted enterprise customers; will sync with SEs.
Alex: handing off to night oncall @Priya in 20min. current status: rollback done, cache trimmed, throttle applied, HPA min raised, p99 ~0.88s (us-west-2). moving to recovery monitoring for 60m. any risks?
Mateo: risk: if we fully re-enable continuous batching without different cache sharding or dedupe we'll hit the same amplification. need a follow-up plan: model-level dedupe + KV prefix limits.
Priya: i'll own postmortem and action items: short-term: add canary guardrail for cache growth > 2x in 15m to auto-revert config. medium: make continuous batching opt-in per-model with quota.
Alex: perfect. i'm leaving a runbook entry in /docs/oncall/runbooks/cache-regression.md and will schedule a meeting with runtime + autoscale next week.
SREBot: Incident acknowledged and tagged: INC-1823045678. severity P2.
Lina: handing update to CS: customers notified.
Priya: taking the pager now, will monitor for 60m then update channel.
Alex: thanks team. if anything spikes call the pager — otherwise i'll pick up postmortem tomorrow. :thumbsup:
